problem.text: The sampler offered top-k and cumulative top-p filtering but no probability cutoff relative to the most likely token.

reasoning.text: SS_MinP retains weights at least min_p times the row maximum. Unlike top-p, it can operate without sorting and does not target a cumulative probability mass.

impact.text: The package exports SS_MinP, and DefaultSampler changes from temperature 0.75 followed by top-p 0.75 to min-p 0.08 followed by temperature 0.8. Existing explicit TopPSampler construction remains unchanged.

source_notes.text: The earlier sampling entry identified a sorted-argmax assignment defect. Inspection of the parent and task diff shows that it is carried over, not corrected by this addition.

Issue #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” concerns extension loading; issue #15, “`cogito-v1-preview-qwen-32B` generates incoherent output for bpw <= 2.5,” concerns quantization regularization. Neither discussion supplies a stated motivation for this sampling change.

limitations: Checks used standard-library binary64 scalar arithmetic, not PyTorch, CUDA, cuRAND or repository execution.
No generation-quality, sampling-frequency or performance measurements establish benefits of the new defaults; the rationale for choosing 0.08 and 0.8 is unestablished.

claims.text: SS_MinP asserts 0 < min_p <= 1. For normalized unsorted probabilities it reduces the last dimension with amax; for normalized sorted probabilities it reads the first column. Both branches multiply by a >= threshold mask and mark the result unnormalized while preserving sortedness and token-index mappings.

Its prep method requests SS_Normalize for raw logits or unnormalized weights. CustomSampler constructs prerequisites using an unchanged INIT planning state, so the new default actually runs normalization, min-p, temperature, then sampling. Normalization converts input logits to float before softmax.

The default cutoff is 8% of the largest probability, not an absolute probability of 0.08. Temperature follows filtering and raises retained weights to 1/0.8 = 1.25, changing their relative weights without changing the already selected support for finite positive inputs.

SS_Sample consumes these unnormalized weights through gumbel_noise_log and torch.argmax. The native wrapper requires matching float tensors; its kernel logs each weight and adds Philox-generated Gumbel noise. No additional normalization or sorting is inserted in the new default.

A scalar transcription on probabilities [0.5, 0.3, 0.125, 0.04, 0.035] produced threshold 0.04, retaining the equality-boundary token and removing only 0.035. Sorted and unsorted masks agreed; min_p=1 retained both tied maxima in [0.4, 0.4, 0.2].

Avoiding the old default's full sort is a plausible computational advantage, but the change also alters truncation semantics and temperature ordering; it is not merely an equivalent faster implementation.

findings.description: The unchanged sorted branches of SS_Argmax do not populate the sample tensor.
findings.trigger: A custom chain reaches SS_Argmax with sorted logits or sorted probabilities, including a sorted min-p composition.
findings.expected_behavior: Map each row's selected position back to its token ID and assign state.sample.
findings.actual_behavior: The branches assign indexed values to state.state, then overwrite it with DONE; state.sample remains None, so forward cannot return its reshaped sample if indexing reaches completion.

verification.description: Whole-parent-tree SS_Argmax search and preset inspection found built-in uses starting directly from INIT. The new default uses SS_Sample, so this observation concerns custom sorted-greedy compositions rather than DefaultSampler.
verification.limits: No repository execution or external custom-caller inventory.

annotation.summary: Adds composable min-p filtering and makes it the default before temperature scaling, replacing default top-p filtering.

argv: p=[0.5,0.3,0.125,0.04,0.035]; t=max(p)*0.08; w=[x if x>=t else 0 for x in p]; q=[x**(1/0.8) for x in w]; print({'threshold':t,'retained':w,'normalized_after_temperature':[x/sum(q) for x in q]}); assert w==[0.5,0.3,0.125,0.04,0]; print('min_p=1 retains ties:',[x for x in [0.4,0.4,0.2] if x>=max([0.4,0.4,0.2])]); print('sorted/unsorted masks agree:', sorted(w,reverse=True)==[x if x>=t else 0 for x in sorted(p,reverse=True)])
